title: Heat, humidity and the World Cup
titleChinese: 世界杯面临高温高湿考验
paragraphs: Around the world, summers are getting hotter. Day and night temperatures are increasing. What impact could that be having on how we sleep?

Temperature and sleep are closely linked. Typically, our bodies cool themselves down before we sleep. One of the main ways that we do this is by widening blood vessels near the skin to allow heat to dissipate. In hot weather, this process becomes less effective as it is more difficult for heat to be transferred. One of the body's mechanisms to speed up this process is by allowing sweat to evaporate. However, in humid conditions it's harder for evaporation to take place. If the body is unable to cool down, then it's more difficult for people to fall asleep and more likely that sleep patterns can be disrupted.

This means that it's important for us to try to manage the temperature of the environment that we sleep in. While it can be costly, air conditioning is a useful tool to keep our sleeping environment cool. Managing ventilation is also important. During the hottest hours of the day keeping windows and curtains closed can stop hot air and heat from sunlight entering our homes. At night, once the temperature has dropped, opening windows can allow cool air to come in and reduce the temperature in our homes. Fans can help to speed up cooling, as long as air temperatures are low enough. They become less effective in hotter conditions.

It's not just rooms that we can cool down. Using breathable bedding and sleepwear makes it easier for our bodies to regulate temperature. While it may seem counter-intuitive, it can be beneficial to have a warm bath or shower before sleep. Warm water can cause more blood to flow to our skin. Once you get out of the bath or shower, this means that you cool down more quickly. Another tip suggested by sleep experts Kevin Morgan and Lisa Artis is to cool your socks in the fridge and then put them on before going to sleep. They also say that it's important to try to keep to your usual sleep routine to avoid disruption to your sleep habits.
chineseParagraphs: 全球范围内，夏季越来越热。白天和夜晚的温度都在升高。这会对我们的睡眠产生什么影响呢？
温度和睡眠密切相关。通常，我们的身体在睡前会自行降温。我们做到这一点的主要方式之一是扩张皮肤附近的血管，让热量散发。在炎热的天气里，这个过程效率降低，因为热量更难传递。身体加速这一过程的机制之一是让汗液蒸发。然而，在潮湿的条件下，蒸发更难发生。如果身体无法降温，那么人们就更难入睡，睡眠模式也更有可能被打乱。
这意味着我们有必要尝试管理睡眠环境的温度。虽然可能成本较高，但空调是保持睡眠环境凉爽的有用工具。管理通风也很重要。在一天中最热的时候，关闭窗户和窗帘可以阻止热空气和阳光热量进入室内。到了晚上，当温度下降后，打开窗户可以让凉爽的空气进入，降低室内温度。只要气温足够低，风扇可以帮助加速冷却。在更热的条件下，风扇的效果会减弱。
我们不仅可以让房间降温。使用透气的床上用品和睡衣能让身体更容易调节温度。虽然看起来可能违反直觉，但睡前洗个温水澡或淋浴可能是有益的。温水能使更多血液流向皮肤。一旦你离开浴缸或淋浴间，这意味着你能更快地降温。睡眠专家凯文·摩根和丽莎·阿蒂斯建议的另一个小技巧是将袜子在冰箱里冷却一下，然后睡前穿上。他们还表示，尽量保持平常的睡眠规律以避免睡眠习惯被打乱也很重要。

vocabulary.definition: 湿度，潮湿（气象学术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: humidity /hjuːˈmɪdəti/ n. 湿度，潮湿（气象学术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The humidity in the tropics is very high.

vocabulary.entry: impact /ˈɪmpækt/ n. 影响，作用
vocabulary.example: The new technology has had a huge impact on the industry.
vocabulary.translation: 这项新技术对该行业产生了巨大影响。

vocabulary.entry: closely /ˈkləʊsli/ adv. 紧密地，密切地
vocabulary.example: The two events are closely connected.

vocabulary.definition: 血管（解剖学术语，固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: blood vessel /ˈblʌd ˌvesl/ n. 血管（解剖学术语，固定表达）
vocabulary.example: High blood pressure can damage blood vessels.

vocabulary.entry: dissipate /ˈdɪsɪpeɪt/ v. 消散，驱散（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The heat dissipated gradually after sunset.

vocabulary.entry: transfer /trænsˈfɜː(r)/ v. 转移，传递
vocabulary.example: The disease can be transferred from animals to humans.
vocabulary.translation: 这种疾病可以从动物传染给人类。

vocabulary.entry: mechanism /ˈmekənɪzəm/ n. 机制，原理（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The mechanism of action of the drug is not fully understood.
vocabulary.translation: 这种药物的作用机制尚未完全了解。

vocabulary.entry: evaporate /ɪˈvæpəreɪt/ v. （使）蒸发（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The water on the ground evaporated in the sun.
vocabulary.translation: 地面上的水在阳光下蒸发了。

vocabulary.entry: humid /ˈhjuːmɪd/ adj. 潮湿的，湿润的
vocabulary.example: The weather was hot and humid.

vocabulary.definition: 蒸发（物理学术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: evaporation /ɪˌvæpəˈreɪʃn/ n. 蒸发（物理学术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Evaporation is a natural process that cools the surface.
vocabulary.translation: 蒸发是冷却表面的自然过程。

vocabulary.entry: disrupt /dɪsˈrʌpt/ v. 打乱，干扰（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The loud noise disrupted my concentration.
vocabulary.translation: 巨大的噪音干扰了我的注意力。

vocabulary.entry: air conditioning /ˈeə kənˌdɪʃənɪŋ/ n. 空调（设备）（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Air conditioning is essential in hot climates.
vocabulary.translation: 空调在炎热气候中是必不可少的。

vocabulary.entry: ventilation /ˌventɪˈleɪʃn/ n. 通风，空气流通（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The room has poor ventilation.

vocabulary.entry: curtain /ˈkɜːtn/ n. 窗帘
vocabulary.example: She drew the curtains to block out the sun.

vocabulary.entry: fan /fæn/ n. 风扇
vocabulary.example: He turned on the fan to cool down.

vocabulary.entry: breathable /ˈbriːðəbl/ adj. 透气的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The fabric is breathable and comfortable.

vocabulary.entry: bedding /ˈbedɪŋ/ n. 床上用品（床单、被褥等）
vocabulary.example: We need to buy new bedding for the guest room.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要为客房买新的床上用品。

vocabulary.entry: sleepwear /ˈsliːpweə(r)/ n. 睡衣（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: She bought new sleepwear for the holiday.

vocabulary.entry: regulate /ˈreɡjuleɪt/ v. 调节，控制（书面语）
vocabulary.example: This drug helps to regulate your heartbeat.
vocabulary.translation: 这种药有助于调节你的心跳。

vocabulary.entry: counter-intuitive /ˌkaʊntər ɪnˈtjuːɪtɪv/ adj. 违反直觉的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: It seems counter-intuitive, but warm water can help you cool down.
vocabulary.translation: 这似乎违反直觉，但温水可以帮助你降温。

vocabulary.entry: sock /sɒk/ n. 短袜
vocabulary.example: He put on a pair of socks before his shoes.
vocabulary.translation: 他在穿鞋前穿上一双袜子。

vocabulary.entry: fridge /frɪdʒ/ n. 冰箱（口语）
vocabulary.example: Put the milk in the fridge.

vocabulary.entry: routine /ruːˈtiːn/ n. 常规，例行程序
vocabulary.example: My morning routine includes a cup of coffee and some reading.
vocabulary.translation: 我早上的例行程序包括一杯咖啡和阅读。

vocabulary.entry: sleep pattern /ˈsliːp ˌpætn/ n. 睡眠模式（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Her sleep patterns changed after she started the new job.
vocabulary.translation: 她开始新工作后，睡眠模式改变了。

vocabulary.entry: disruption /dɪsˈrʌpʃn/ n. 中断，扰乱（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The power outage caused a disruption in communication.

vocabulary.definition: 气温，空气温度（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: air temperature /ˈeə ˌtemprətʃə(r)/ n. 气温，空气温度（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The air temperature dropped below zero.

vocabulary.entry: sunlight /ˈsʌnlaɪt/ n. 阳光
vocabulary.example: Sunlight streamed through the window.
